items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs, by rearranging variables from different sources into a single new data matrix placed one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the planned augmented-matrix approach for merging NIR and Raman spectra from the same spot; in the feasibility study, the fused model should be benchmarked against the best single-method model on held-out runs before committing to a second instrument.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The review is general PAT literature, not yeast fermentation or NIR/Raman specifically, and it does not state that fusion improves performance, only how it is structured.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: The review states that before fusing data from multiple sources, the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity must be evaluated.
items.how_it_applies: This justifies keeping each method's own calibration and diagnostics during the study and checking whether the second instrument adds predictive value before it is kept.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: It is a general recommendation from a review, not a validated result for NIR plus Raman in fermenting broth, so the actual benefit must be demonstrated on the customer's own runs.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: The review cites a Raman and FT-IR food analytical study in which instrument complementarity alone was not sufficient to improve the prediction of several CQAs.
items.how_it_applies: This is a caution that adding a second spectroscopy method may not improve predictions, so the feasibility study should include the pre-defined condition that the fused model must beat the best single method or the second instrument is dropped.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited example is a food application with Raman and FT-IR, not NIR and Raman in yeast fermentation, so the outcome there does not predict the result here.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E02 ¶36

items.finding: The review states that the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This links the auxiliary temperature measurement to the optical measurement itself: broth temperature should be recorded during the study because temperature variation can affect the NIR spectra used for biomass and metabolite models.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns NIR and MIR spectroscopy of aqueous solutions generally, with tempered sample holders, whereas the customer's application is in-line measurement in fermenting broth without such holders, so the impact must be assessed under real process conditions.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

dropped.finding: The document's table of contents lists temperature as a standard measured parameter alongside pH, dissolved oxygen and biomass within its fermentation monitoring section.
dropped.how_it_applies: This indicates that temperature is commonly monitored as an auxiliary parameter in fermentation setups, supporting inclusion of a temperature sensor in the feasibility study design; the actual sensor type and placement should be tested on the customer's vessel.
dropped.limits_and_transfer_risks: The quote is only a table of contents entry from a 2007 micro-bioreactor sensor array thesis, so it shows that temperature was covered but gives no performance, method or accuracy details, and the setup (micro bioreactors) differs from a production-scale fermentation.
